objective: Develop an independent municipal model with demonstrably better out-of-sample forecasts than SKR on matched targets.
role: External benchmark only. Do not insert SKR forecast outputs into candidate predictions.

comparisonScope.publicWorkbooks: Municipal tax and grant revenue benchmarks. Not the full budget model or its source code.
comparisonScope.wholeBudget: Requires separately archived comparable budget-model outputs; revenue-only results cannot establish whole-budget superiority.

findings: Revenue categories are separately modelled; compare reconciled tax and grant definitions including settlements and property fees (printed pages 11-13).
The public forecast workbook is a default-output reconciliation reference, distinct from the complete model (printed page 7).
National tax-base level forecast evaluation, not a municipal whole-budget accuracy score.
Use absolute errors and bias; national percentage errors cannot be compared directly with municipal errors in mnkr.

historicalArchive.note: The 25:59 circular links to the current forecast page; this does not recover the original 2025 workbook.

acceptanceProtocol.primaryCriterion: Lower held-out mean absolute error than SKR and simple persistence/trend baselines on the same cases.
controls: Archive original source releases, model version and input provenance.
Separate development, tuning and final evaluation periods; lock specifications before final evaluation.
Refit using only data available at each forecast origin. Metadata checks do not prove an actual historical cutoff.
Keep target years intact when assessing uncertainty; forecasts for the same outcome are correlated.
Report missing cases and per-horizon errors; do not select only winning targets.
Future-year differences without outcomes are scenario differences, not accuracy evidence.
acceptanceProtocol.claimRule: A lower error on a small sample is descriptive evidence only, not proof of general superiority.

currentEvidence.kind: Retrospective population comparison only; not a SKR comparison.

nextModelHypotheses: Local employment and taxable income dynamics beyond population ratios.
Finer elderly cohorts and observed care intensity.
Sector-specific cost and capacity adjustment estimated from historical observations.
